title: primary_iso3_dropped's second entry did not close its gap -- it left the sensor's field of view: gdacs-tc-1001305 closed tonight with the CHN divergence still uncorrected, and the check will never examine it again
statement: foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-25/run.json's primary_iso3_dropped shrank from two entries last night (gdacs-dr-1027450/ERI, gdacs-tc-1001305/CHN) back to one (gdacs-dr-1027450/ERI only). This is not the gap closing. gdacs-tc-1001305 was CLOSED_BY_SOURCE tonight (foreknown/registry.json futures['gdacs-tc-1001305'].history, event CLOSED_BY_SOURCE at 2026-08-25T06:04:45+00:00; also listed in foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-25/run.json's closed array) with its committed iso3 permanently ['JPN'] while its committed where still reads 'Northern Mariana Islands, Japan, China' -- the same divergence obs-2026-08-24-1.json and the 2026-08-24 review of sensor-primary-iso3-gap.json described the night before, now frozen at closure rather than corrected. The reason the run-summary entry disappeared is mechanical, not evidential: practice/src/practice/foreknown/run.py's primary_iso3_dropped loop (the code implementing sensor-primary-iso3-gap.json) only iterates parsed_feeds['GDACS']['features'] -- tonight's raw feed -- looking up each feature's own eventid against the registry. foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-25/gdacs.json's 95 features do not include eventid 1001305 (confirmed by direct membership check); a future that leaves the source's feed is exactly how futures.py's update_registry (practice/src/practice/foreknown/futures.py, line 231) already decides CLOSED_BY_SOURCE. Once a future stops appearing in the feed, the loop has nothing to compare for it, so it can neither add it to nor keep it out of primary_iso3_dropped on its own evidence -- it simply stops being looked at, forever, since CLOSED futures do not reopen into the feed. The gap in the committed record (iso3 missing a country the future's own where text names) is now permanent and will never again be flagged by the sensor that exists to flag exactly this.
method: Diffed foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-24/run.json against foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-25/run.json's primary_iso3_dropped field (python3 json diff), finding gdacs-tc-1001305/CHN present the first night and absent the second. Read foreknown/registry.json's futures['gdacs-tc-1001305'] to find the CLOSED_BY_SOURCE history event and confirm committed iso3 stayed ['JPN'] through closure while where still names China. Read foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-25/run.json's closed array, confirming gdacs-tc-1001305 is listed there tonight. Read practice/src/practice/foreknown/run.py's primary_iso3_dropped block (implementing sensor-primary-iso3-gap.json) to find it iterates only parsed_feeds['GDACS']['features'], and practice/src/practice/foreknown/futures.py line 231 to confirm CLOSED_BY_SOURCE is itself derived from a future's absence from the feed. Loaded foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-25/gdacs.json and checked eventid 1001305 against the 95 features' eventids (python3), confirming it is absent from tonight's raw feed -- the mechanical reason the check no longer sees it.
worth_watching_because: The 2026-08-24 review of sensor-primary-iso3-gap.json named the open question as whether the registry-side gap is a standing cause; tonight adds a different fact about the sensor itself, not about the gap's cause -- the sensor's own visibility is bounded by the source's feed, so a divergence can be caught while OPEN and then vanish from the running record's attention the moment the future closes, without ever being corrected. sensor-primary-iso3-gap.json's falsification clause already treats primary_iso3_dropped staying empty as evidence the underlying cause is gone; tonight shows a second, unrelated way the list can shrink -- a case leaving the check's field of view rather than the gap being fixed -- that the falsification clause does not distinguish from genuine resolution. Any future reading of 'the list is empty tonight' as reassuring needs to know both readings are possible from the same figure.
left_alone: Not proposing a new sensor -- this is a property of sensor-primary-iso3-gap.json's existing check (its dependence on feed presence), not a new phenomenon needing its own instrument; recorded as a review addition to that proposal file instead. Not changing run.py to also scan CLOSED futures for a stale iso3 gap at closure time (or to snapshot the gap into the CLOSED_BY_SOURCE history event) -- that would be a real fix for the blind spot this observation names, but it is a code and possibly a registry-schema change or the sort the 2026-08-20 review already flagged as a design question for the maintainer (iso3 is not a TRACKED_FIELD; making the closure event carry a final iso3-vs-where diff is a similar-shaped decision), not something one observation's evidence settles unilaterally. Not touching the three PROPOSED sensors (lead-time-pathway-idle, registry-stall, source-reconfirmation-blind-spot) -- lead-time-pathway-idle still has exactly 2 of the 10 FORECAST-kind resolutions its test_rule waits for (foreknown/resolutions/nhc-al032026.json, foreknown/resolutions/nhc-ep082026.json; unchanged since last night), and the other two both carry open reviews asking for a firing-rule redesign, not more nights of the same data. Not writing a memoryhole/verdicts file -- the newest reading, memoryhole/readings/2026-08-24.json, carries zero rule-layer abstentions across all 20 entries.
